title: Rulers, Authorities and Powers
lead: Paul's lists of "rulers, authorities, powers and lordships" name beings or forces above the human level (Ephesians 1:21; 3:10; 6:12; Colossians 1:16; 2:15; Romans 8:38). Most readers take them as angelic and demonic powers; some also include the structures of human society. Christ is above them all.

sections.b: The terms come from Jewish thought about the heavenly world, where nations had patron angels (Deuteronomy 32:8 in the Septuagint; Daniel 10:13, 20-21). Paul can speak of them as created through Christ (Colossians 1:16), as defeated at the cross (Colossians 2:15), as unable to separate believers from God's love (Romans 8:38), and as hostile (Ephesians 6:12). Readings: personal spirits (the older church view, and Clinton Arnold's study of Ephesus and its magic); the structures of society, such as law, money and the state (Hendrikus Berkhof, John Howard Yoder); both an outer structure and an inner spirit (Walter Wink).
